audience: Cursor is for people who want an editor with deep codebase context, tab completion, and an agent that can use more than one frontier model. That product description is the pros list, and it is why people compare it with Copilot and Claude Code. The verdict is not about the editor being bad. It is about the price list.

Buy it only if you can stand a Depends rating. On 14 October 2026 the docs still listed Pro at $20, Pro Plus at $60, and Ultra at $200. The public pricing page did not list those names or those dollar amounts. If you need the checkout to match the docs before you pay, wait.
features: Deep codebase context and a strong agent are the features people are actually buying. Multiple frontier models are the other pro. None of that is in dispute. The dispute is which plan name you type into a budget.

The table on this page is docs-sourced and unconfirmed. cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing, which the older account pricing URL redirects to, says Pro $20 a month, Pro Plus $60 a month, and Ultra $200 a month. That is the only price table we print.
Usage past the included pool is pay-as-you-go. The cons say so, and they do not give the overage rate. We do not invent one. A plan price is the start of the invoice if you leave the pool.
limitations: The public page, cursor.com/pricing, returned HTTP 200 with the title Cursor · Pricing and did not redirect. It did not list Pro, Pro Plus, or the docs dollar amounts. It listed Free at $0 a month, Plus at $8 a month, Premium at $30 a month, Super at $100 a month, Ultra at $200 a month, and Teams at $30+ per user a month, mixed with Grok and X features. Those tiers are not shown in our table. Do not treat that public lineup as Cursor's plan list, and do not treat the docs list as the page a buyer sees today.
Ultra at $200 appears in both places, which is not the same as the lineups matching. The names around it do not match. A shared number is not a confirmation.
The rating is Depends, and last verified is empty, because we will not stamp a date on a price the two official pages disagree about. The verdict stays the mismatch.
